entry.title: Authenticating WebSocket connections at the edge
entry.summary:
Authenticating WebSocket connections at the edge
A WebSocket session begins as an ordinary HTTP request and stops being one after the server answers with 101 Switching Protocols. Authentication middleware, reverse proxies and web application firewalls get one chance to inspect that request. After the upgrade they see a long-lived TCP connection carrying frames they usually do not parse. Teams that protect REST endpoints carefully often leave the socket path to whatever the framework does by default. RFC 6455 defines the opening handshake, including Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Key and Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13. Because the handshake is an HTTP request, it carries cookies and an Authorization header when the client chooses to send them. That is where a session check belongs. Origin h…

entry.summary: To monitor cron job silent failure, use app logs and an external heartbeat together, then keep a durable run record that survives rollback.
